name: andBEYOND Phinda Private Game
positioning: andBeyond Phinda Private Game Reserve: a Big Five private reserve with six lodges across seven habitats in the Munywana Conservancy, KwaZulu-Natal
best_for: Travellers who want a Big Five safari with the Indian Ocean coast a short drive away
Guests drawn to walking safaris and a land restored from farmland to wilderness

facts.text: Phinda Private Game Reserve is set within the Munywana Conservancy in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
Phinda spans 29,866 hectares (73,800 acres) across seven distinct habitats.
Phinda's habitats range from rare sand forest and savanna to wetland and woodland.
Phinda is home to the Big Five, along with cheetah, hyena, giraffe, nyala, zebra and more than 400 bird species.
The reserve is home to six lodges, each designed to reflect its own setting.
Phinda's land had endured almost a century dominated by pineapple, cattle and sisal farms.
A significant portion of the land has been returned to its ancestral owners in a partnership between andBeyond and the neighbouring Makhasa and Mnqobokazi communities.
Phinda offers a variety of walking safaris.
Guests can cycle through the rare sand forest on a guided e-bike excursion.
Phinda offers a boating experience on the Mzinene River.
Phinda Rock Lodge suites are built from contoured stone and open onto a private deck and plunge pool.

highlights.text: Phinda limits vehicles, with sightings of cheetah, black rhino, elephant and the shy suni antelope.
Phinda Forest Lodge is set within one of Africa's last remaining dry sand forests.
Phinda Rock Lodge is set into the cliff face above the valley.
Marine encounters at Phinda range from turtle nesting adventures to ocean safaris and scuba diving.
The reserve is a short drive from the beaches and coral reefs of the Indian Ocean.

considerations.text: Phinda is in a low-risk malaria area; travellers should consult their healthcare provider before travel.
The reserve is reached via a private airstrip exclusive to andBeyond guests, or by road from Durban, Richards Bay or Johannesburg.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires connecting flights.
